# Requirements

Let Neo work UNPROMPTED. During normal conversation Neo quietly captures things the user mentioned needing/wanting or that would clearly benefit them but did NOT explicitly ask Neo to do — durable 'opportunities'. Then, while the user is idle (the per-user daemon has scaled to zero between requests), Neo RANDOMLY wakes, picks one eligible opportunity, does the work autonomously, and pings the user with the finished result: a pleasant surprise, not a request fulfilled. The feature is mostly additive over substrate that already exists: capture rides the per-turn background consolidation pass (neo/internal/writeback/consolidator.go); idle wake rides Chronos (the centralized durable agent alarm-clock that already wakes a scaled-to-zero daemon by injecting a /chat turn via router POST /internal/wake) as a sibling of the existing heartbeat convention (chronos/internal/heartbeat <-> neo/internal/agent/heartbeat.go) carrying an AUTOMATRIX marker; execution rides the existing supervised, connection-decoupled, restart-durable task engine (neo/internal/server/session.go drive/superviseTask); only the outbound notify seam is genuinely new (a pluggable Notifier: default ntfy, optional Apprise fan-out, plus a durable in-app automatrix.complete record). LOCKED decisions: autonomy boundary = FULL NON-FINANCIAL (the only hard exclusion is financial/on-chain, enforced STRUCTURALLY via a restricted tool surface that omits the money/chain core_execute path — respecting frozen invariant i1 'Neo never signs' + Chronos i5 'off-chain only'); rollout = OPT-IN (Settings toggle, default OFF; capture runs silently regardless so the queue is warm, but Neo never wakes to work until enabled); honesty = an Automatrix turn passes the SAME Cassandra completion gate as any state-touching turn — Neo never pings a result it did not genuinely produce. These requirements trace to the approved design (rendered into design.md).

## Requirement 1: Capture implicit opportunities from conversation

**User Story:** As a user, I want Neo to notice the helpful things I mention in passing but don't formally ask for, so that they aren't forgotten and can be acted on later.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE per-turn background consolidation pass (neo/internal/writeback/consolidator.go) SHALL, in addition to its existing extractions, extract an `opportunities` class: specific, actionable things the user implied wanting or would clearly benefit from but did NOT explicitly ask Neo to do this turn.
2. THE extraction SHALL require each opportunity to be grounded in something the user actually said or did (a `rationale` citing it), SHALL drop vague or low-confidence items below a configured confidence floor, and SHALL be selective by default (most turns yield none — the correct, common outcome).
3. A direct request the user made this turn (already being handled) SHALL NOT be captured as an opportunity, so the queue holds only unrequested, proactive work.
4. EACH captured opportunity SHALL carry a first-pass `financial` classification (true for anything involving spending, sending value, trading, or on-chain writes) supplied by the extraction model.
5. THE capture pass SHALL run whenever the feature is built in, INDEPENDENT of the per-user opt-in state, so the opportunity queue is already warm if and when the user enables proactive execution.

## Requirement 2: Durable, deduplicated opportunity queue in cortex

**User Story:** As the system, I want captured opportunities stored durably with a clear lifecycle, so that they survive restarts, don't pile up duplicates, and can be ranked for autonomous work.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH accepted opportunity SHALL be written to cortex as a durable record carrying at least: summary (actionable, self-sufficient), rationale, status, eligible_autonomous (bool), confidence, origin_conversation_id, created_at/updated_at, and attempts.
2. THE opportunity status SHALL follow the lifecycle pending -> scheduled -> in_progress -> done | dismissed, and status transitions SHALL be persisted atomically so a restart never loses or double-runs an item.
3. A newly captured opportunity SHALL be deduplicated against existing pending opportunities (normalize + semantic similarity, the same discipline as RememberFact) so a repeatedly-mentioned need does not accumulate duplicates.
4. THE pager SHALL expose a reader that returns ONLY eligible-autonomous, pending opportunities, ranked (confidence x salience x recency), for the autonomous picker; and a writer to set an opportunity's status.
5. THE opportunity records SHALL be scoped to the owning user/agent and SHALL NOT store secrets, tokens, or private keys.

## Requirement 3: Non-financial autonomy boundary (structural guarantee)

**User Story:** As a user, I want absolute certainty that Neo's unprompted work can never spend my money or move value, so that I can trust it to act while I'm away.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. NO financial or on-chain action SHALL ever be performed by an autonomous Automatrix run; the ONLY hard exclusion on otherwise-permitted autonomous work is financial/on-chain.
2. THE autonomous run SHALL execute on a RESTRICTED tool surface (built via the existing sub-agent RestrictTools mechanism) that OMITS the money/chain core_execute delegate entirely, so a run physically cannot reach the signing path regardless of model intent or a mis-classified item.
3. THE autonomous opportunity picker SHALL only ever select opportunities flagged eligible_autonomous (non-financial); a financial opportunity SHALL NEVER be auto-run.
4. WHERE the extraction model's financial flag is uncertain or missing, THE system SHALL apply a deterministic re-check on the opportunity summary and SHALL fail closed (treat as financial / not eligible) when in doubt.
5. A financial opportunity SHALL still be CAPTURED and SHALL be SURFACED to the user for explicit approval (where it runs as a normal, gated, user-initiated task), but SHALL never be executed without that explicit approval.

## Requirement 4: Random idle wake via Chronos (the AUTOMATRIX alarm)

**User Story:** As a user, I want Neo to pick up proactive work during my downtime without me prompting it, at unpredictable-feeling times, so that it never competes with my active use.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user enables Automatrix, THE per-user daemon SHALL create exactly ONE recurring AUTOMATRIX alarm via the Chronos MCP tool (alarm_set); WHEN the user disables it, THE daemon SHALL cancel that alarm.
2. THE AUTOMATRIX wake SHALL be delivered by the existing Chronos -> router POST /internal/wake -> daemon /chat path (origin=chronos, alarm_id), and Neo SHALL detect it via an AUTOMATRIX wake marker (a sibling of the existing HEARTBEAT marker) distinct from a normal user message.
3. THE wake cadence SHALL feel random rather than clockwork: the engine SHALL reschedule the next wake with randomized jitter within a configured window (and MAY probabilistically skip a fire), while Chronos remains the durable timing backbone (state in Postgres, not memory).
4. ON each wake, THE engine SHALL re-read the per-user opt-in setting and SHALL do nothing (and cancel the alarm) if the user has opted out since the alarm was created.
5. ON each wake, IF a run is already in flight for the user (the session is busy), THE engine SHALL NOT start proactive work and SHALL defer (reschedule) — Automatrix never interrupts or competes with real user work.
6. IF there is no eligible pending opportunity, THE wake turn SHALL resolve to an idle sentinel (AUTOMATRIX_IDLE) that is SUPPRESSED (no output/surface), exactly like the heartbeat HEARTBEAT_OK suppression, and the next wake SHALL be rescheduled.
7. THE number of proactive tasks started SHALL be bounded per day by a configured cap (anti-spam).

## Requirement 5: Autonomous execution of one opportunity

**User Story:** As a user, I want Neo to actually complete a helpful task end-to-end while I'm idle, picking up the full context of where the need arose, so that what I get back is a finished, genuinely-useful result.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ON a wake with work to do, THE engine SHALL select the single highest-ranked eligible opportunity, mark it scheduled->in_progress, and dispatch a supervised run (session.drive/superviseTask) that is decoupled from any user connection and durable across restart (the Task Durability Rule).
2. THE run SHALL resume into the opportunity's origin_conversation_id so Neo regains the relevant thread transcript + cortex memory (context fidelity), and SHALL build its working objective from the opportunity summary + rationale.
3. THE run SHALL execute on the restricted (non-financial) tool surface from req.3 and SHALL be bounded by the normal task wall-clock and step budget.
4. THE autonomous turn SHALL be held to the SAME completion gate (Cassandra adjudicator / deterministic grounding) as any state-touching turn; it SHALL be considered done ONLY when it genuinely passes the gate.
5. ON genuine completion, THE engine SHALL mark the opportunity done; ON a partial or failed attempt, THE engine SHALL leave it pending (incrementing attempts, bounded), surface NOTHING to the user (no failed-surprise spam), and allow a later wake to retry or eventually dismiss it.

## Requirement 6: Completion ping — ntfy/Apprise + durable in-app record

**User Story:** As a user, I want to be pleasantly surprised with a notification when Neo finishes something for me, even if the app is closed, and to always find the result waiting in the app.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ON genuine completion of an autonomous task, THE system SHALL write a DURABLE in-app record (an automatrix.complete event + sidecar) capturing the opportunity summary, a result summary, the conversation id, a created_at, and an unread flag — the canonical, replayable surface regardless of external delivery.
2. THE system SHALL deliver an out-of-app ping through a pluggable Notifier whose DEFAULT backend is ntfy (POST to /, with a per-user topic derived from the agent DID or set by config), and whose OPTIONAL backend is Apprise (APPRISE_URL or the apprise CLI) for fan-out to other services.
3. WHERE no notifier is configured, THE system SHALL fall back to a no-op external send while STILL writing the durable in-app record, so a result is never lost.
4. EXTERNAL delivery SHALL be best-effort and SHALL NEVER block the agent loop; a failed external send SHALL be logged and SHALL NOT be reported to the user as delivered (honest failure), while the in-app record remains.
5. THE notification and in-app surfaces SHALL show the RESULT, not the protocol — no Chronos/alarm/marker/cortex jargon — consistent with the consumer-product rule.

## Requirement 7: Opt-in control + opportunity management UI

**User Story:** As a user, I want to turn proactive Neo on or off and see/curate what it's considering, so that I'm always in control of unprompted behavior.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE proactive behavior SHALL be OPT-IN: a per-user setting (default OFF) stored in the per-user daemon settings governs whether Neo wakes to work; the engine SHALL treat this setting as authoritative on every wake.
2. THE client SHALL provide a Settings -> Automatrix section with the master toggle and a plain-language explanation (Neo occasionally works on helpful things you mentioned and tells you when done; never anything that spends money), following UI house rules (separation by background-color contrast, never border strokes; no emojis, gradients, or glow).
3. THE client SHALL present a queue view of pending opportunities where the user can DISMISS an item (status->dismissed) or APPROVE a financial item for a normal, gated, user-initiated run.
4. THE client SHALL present the completion inbox / unread badge from req.6 so the surprise results are discoverable on next open.
5. TOGGLING the setting ON SHALL cause the AUTOMATRIX alarm to be created and OFF SHALL cause it to be cancelled (req.4.1), with the change taking effect without a process restart.

## Requirement 8: Safety, ownership, and honesty boundaries

**User Story:** As the system owner, I want Automatrix to be scoped, off-chain, honest, and non-spammy, so that an autonomous feature cannot be abused or erode trust.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE AUTOMATRIX alarm SHALL be DID-scoped per Chronos (an agent only creates/lists/cancels its own alarms; the wake target derives from the verified DID), and Automatrix SHALL perform NO on-chain action and hold NO signing key (Chronos i5/i7; frozen invariant i1).
2. AUTOMATRIX SHALL NOT modify the signed MCL walk (compile/plan/walk/synthesize/critic/emitFinalTurn, D11 byte-identity) and SHALL NOT grant Chronos any new signing/cortex/plan-walk capability — Chronos only delivers a /chat turn; Neo does the work.
3. NEO SHALL NEVER fabricate that a proactive task was completed; a ping SHALL be sent only after the completion gate genuinely accepts (req.5.4), and partial/failed work is never announced as done.
4. AUTOMATRIX SHALL respect the per-day task cap and SHALL defer on a busy session (req.4.5/4.7), so proactive work cannot spam the user or starve real work.
5. NO secrets, tokens, private keys, or .env values SHALL be stored in opportunity records, notifications, or the durable completion sidecar.

## Requirement 9: Real verification — no fakes

**User Story:** As the system owner, I want Automatrix proven against real code paths, so that capture, gating, idle wake, execution, and notify genuinely work before it ships.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE feature SHALL verify capture against the REAL consolidator extraction: a transcript with an implied need yields a real cortex Opportunity record; a transcript without one yields none; a direct request is not captured.
2. THE feature SHALL verify the non-financial guarantee against real code: a financial opportunity is never returned by the eligible-pending reader, and the restricted tool surface really lacks the money core_execute tool (assert the actual schema set), failing closed on uncertain classification.
3. THE feature SHALL verify the wake path against real code: the AUTOMATRIX marker is detected, AUTOMATRIX_IDLE suppresses the turn, a busy session defers, and an opted-out user is refused.
4. THE feature SHALL verify notify against a real ntfy backend (httptest round-trip) and that the durable in-app record is written and marked unread; a failed external send still leaves the record.
5. THE feature SHALL verify the opt-in lifecycle: enabling creates the alarm and disabling cancels it, and the engine refuses proactive work when the setting is off.
6. NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a stub/mock/fake for a real code path or type to manufacture a pass.
